BlankSeparated.expectation: split at gap_tolerance=0; merged at gap_tolerance>=1
BlankSeparated.shape: two tables separated by exactly one blank row

DuplicateHeaders.expectation: header values alone cannot separate the tables by position; only the range can
DuplicateHeaders.shape: two tables with identical header VALUES (Port, 2023, 2024) but in different column order in the second table

HiddenAxes.expectation: hidden axes are reported per address; the two tables differ in column width (3 then 2), so their bounds differ
HiddenAxes.shape: column C hidden and row 4 hidden; two stacked tables

MergedCells.expectation: merge ranges are read; covered addresses are reported as merge-covered rather than absent
MergedCells.shape: merged title A1:C1 and merged row label A2:A3

RaggedRows.expectation: ragged row detection; B2 empty, C2 absent
RaggedRows.shape: row 2 is short of the region width

SideBySide.expectation: KNOWN LIMITATION: the detector groups by row, so two side-by-side tables become one region spanning both, with the blank separator reported as an empty column
SideBySide.shape: two tables on the same rows, in different column ranges

SingleTable.expectation: one region; address is a sufficient identity because nothing else in the sheet looks like a table

TwinSameSheet.expectation: the strongest ambiguity case: header values identical, content fingerprint identical, only the address differs
TwinSameSheet.shape: two tables with byte-identical content at different addresses in the same sheet

TwoAdjacentTables.expectation: the detector should not see a row gap, so it emits ONE region spanning both tables and the region bounds do not correspond to either real table
TwoAdjacentTables.shape: two tables stacked with no separating blank row and a changed column structure (3 columns then 2)
